initiatives.name: NPF Åland
initiatives.summary: Åland Islands association spreading knowledge about neuropsychiatric disabilities and advocating for the rights of people with them, running member support groups and a youth forum called Simuli.
initiatives.notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations. Affiliated with Funktionsrätt Åland and ABF Åland.

initiatives.name: Albanian Children Foundation
initiatives.summary: A Tirana-based Albanian charity working on child health broadly, which runs a National Center for Autism and related training and awareness campaigns in Tirana, Farkë, Kukës and Tetova.
initiatives.notes: Autism-Europe affiliated member, listed under 'Associated Members' as Albania's representative. The organisation's overall remit is broader child-health humanitarian work (also covering thalassemia and general child welfare); autism is one dedicated programme (its National Center for Autism), not its sole focus. Included for country diversity; flagged here for editorial review.

initiatives.name: AUTEA (Andorra Autism Association)
initiatives.summary: Andorra's national autism association, based in Andorra la Vella, listed as a full member of Autism-Europe representing autistic people and families in the microstate.
initiatives.notes: Site returned no readable content to automated fetch (likely a JS-rendered page) despite a live 202 response; existence and details drawn from Autism-Europe's official August 2026 member directory. Founding year and leadership composition unconfirmed.

initiatives.name: DISFAM Argentina
initiatives.summary: The Argentine chapter of the international DISFAM dyslexia network, raising awareness of dyslexia and other learning disabilities and pushing schools and education ministries toward detection and support protocols since 2013.
initiatives.notes: Founded by parents, teachers and health professionals; part of the Spain-headquartered international DISFAM network, not an independent Argentine organization.

initiatives.name: Frente de Artistas del Borda
initiatives.summary: Arts collective founded in 1984 inside Buenos Aires' Borda psychiatric hospital, made up of current and former patients working alongside community members and professionals across theatre, music, and visual-arts workshops.
initiatives.notes: Blog itself dormant since ~2012, but org's continued activity confirmed via 40th-anniversary (2024) press coverage and a live YouTube channel. A commonly cited domain, frentedeartistasdelbord.com, does not resolve (dead).

initiatives.name: FUBIPA (Argentine Bipolar Foundation)
initiatives.name_local: Fundación Bipolares de la República Argentina
initiatives.summary: A Buenos Aires mutual-aid foundation for people with bipolar disorder and their families, running free peer support groups since 1989 alongside professional-led psychoeducation workshops.
initiatives.notes: Founded by two psychiatrists, two people with bipolar disorder, and a family member; describes itself as the oldest volunteer association for serious mental disorders in Latin America. Peer-run mutual-aid groups; governing council traditionally chaired by a professional.

initiatives.name: Mad in Argentina
initiatives.summary: An editorial platform on mad culture, mental health and neurodiversity in Argentina, part of the international Mad in the World network, publishing essays and interviews from activists, journalists and a national disability-agency staffer.
initiatives.notes: Team includes a self-described Latin American mad-movement activist alongside journalists; actively publishing as of September 2026.

initiatives.name: Mad Pride Buenos Aires (Orgullo Loco)
initiatives.summary: A Buenos Aires platform of mutual support and activism run by neurodivergent and psychiatric-survivor people, organizing around Mad Pride to contest psychiatric stigma, pathologization and institutionalization.
initiatives.notes: Self-describes as a platform of association and mutual support formed by neurodivergent people; corroborated by Pikara Magazine and academic literature on the Latin American Orgullo Loco movement. Facebook is its only confirmed public presence.

initiatives.name: Amaze
initiatives.summary: Victoria's peak autism body, providing information, advocacy, and support for autistic people and their families.
initiatives.notes: Board includes at least one autistic member alongside parents of autistic adults; not stated as autistic-led.

initiatives.name: Arts Project Australia
initiatives.summary: Arts Project Australia is a Melbourne studio and gallery founded in 1974 by Myra Hilgendorf, the first full-time art studio in Australia dedicated to artists with intellectual disability, now supporting more than 150 artists.
initiatives.notes: Site's own tagline calls itself an organisation 'championing neurodivergent artists and artists with intellectual disability.'

initiatives.name: Autism CRC (Cooperative Research Centre for Living with Autism)
initiatives.summary: University of Queensland-based Australian research centre, established in 2013, co-funding participatory autism research and programmes such as the DXC Dandelion employment programme.
initiatives.notes: Academic-run, not self-advocate-led.

initiatives.name: Autistic Self Advocacy Network Australia and New Zealand (ASAN AUNZ)
initiatives.summary: Grassroots autistic-led advocacy network doing systemic advocacy and self-advocacy skill-building across Australia and New Zealand.
initiatives.notes: Binational (Australia and New Zealand); member of the Australian Autism Alliance; organisationally distinct from ASAN in the USA.

initiatives.name: Back to Back Theatre
initiatives.summary: Contemporary theatre company in Geelong whose ensemble consists of actors with disability; founded 1987, led by non-disabled Artistic Director Bruce Gladwin with a full-time disabled ensemble at its creative core.
initiatives.notes: Ensemble members are neurodivergent/disabled; Artistic Director Bruce Gladwin is not disclosed as disabled. No 'led by disabled people' claim found on site.

initiatives.name: DXC Dandelion Program
initiatives.summary: Corporate autism employment initiative run by DXC Technology since 2014, in partnership with universities and Autism CRC, with 17 teams and over 250 autistic employees across Australia.
initiatives.notes: Reports 92% retention rate among autistic employees; a corporate CSR programme, not autistic-led.

initiatives.name: I CAN Network
initiatives.summary: Autistic-led group mentoring organisation delivering school-based and online mentoring programmes for autistic and neurodivergent young people in Australia and New Zealand.
initiatives.notes: Founder is autistic; reports 77% of staff are autistic and requires a minimum of half; reaches both Australia and New Zealand.

initiatives.name: Rawcus
initiatives.summary: Melbourne ensemble theatre company creating devised performance work with an ensemble of performers with and without disability.
initiatives.notes: Originated via a partnership between Theatreworks, disability organisation Scope, and the City of Port Phillip. Site returns 406 to a bare curl user agent.

initiatives.name: Reframing Autism
initiatives.summary: Australian registered charity providing education, resources, courses, and advocacy on autism, run by and for autistic people.
initiatives.notes: Operates nationally with no single fixed HQ city stated; registered with the ACNC.

initiatives.name: Restless Dance Theatre
initiatives.summary: Adelaide-based inclusive contemporary dance company founded in 1991 by Sally Chance and Tania Rose, building careers for disabled and neurodivergent dancers.
initiatives.notes: Founded by non-disabled artists. Company's own history notes a former artistic director (2009) was 'the first artistic director with a disability in any Australian dance company', and current AD Michelle Ryan (since 2013) has MS — but no blanket 'disability-led' institutional claim, so kept as mixed.

initiatives.name: Studio A
initiatives.summary: Studio A is a supported studio based in St Leonards, Sydney, led by CEO/Artistic Director Gabrielle Mordy, providing professional development and commercial representation to artists with intellectual disability.
initiatives.notes: Founding year not stated on the mission/impact pages checked; could not verify this session.

initiatives.name: Yellow Ladybugs
initiatives.summary: Autistic-led Australian organisation running community events, education, and advocacy for autistic girls, women, and gender-diverse people.
initiatives.notes: CEO/founder is autistic; site states it is 'proudly autistic-led and neuro affirming'.

initiatives.name: Austrian Autism Aid (ÖAH)
initiatives.summary: A Vienna-based nonprofit that grew out of a parents' self-help group into Austria's federal coordination centre for autism, offering free family counselling, diagnostics, therapy, job coaching, and specialist training.
initiatives.notes: Not an Autism-Europe member as of the August 2026 directory (Austria has no listed AE member); found independently as Austria's national coordination and advocacy body. Explicitly emerged from a parent self-help group. Founding year not stated on the site.

initiatives.name: Austrian Federal Association for Dyslexia (ÖBVL)
initiatives.summary: Austrian dyslexia association providing certified training for dyslexia therapists, professional continuing education, therapist directories and public information on dyslexia.
initiatives.notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Headquarters city not stated on the site; Vienna used as a national placeholder.

initiatives.name: Museum Gugging
initiatives.summary: Art brut complex in Maria Gugging (Klosterneuburg) built around the Haus der Künstler, a residence-studio for artists with psychiatric/intellectual disabilities opened 1981 under psychiatrist Leo Navratil; the museum building dates to 2006.
initiatives.notes: Museum itself operated by NÖ Museum Betriebs GmbH under artistic director Johann Feilacher (psychiatrist), not by the resident artists. The adjacent galerie gugging (separate site, galeriegugging.com) is owned by the Gugging Artists collective — worth a separate look if a more nd-led entry is wanted.

initiatives.name: The Society for the Welfare of Autistic Children (SWAC)
initiatives.summary: Dhaka-based nonprofit founded in 2000 by parents of autistic individuals, running a school, therapy services, respite care, and a social enterprise for people with autism.
initiatives.notes: Executive Committee is mainly composed of parents of autistic individuals.

initiatives.name: Collectif Autiste de Belgique
initiatives.summary: A peer-support collective created by and for autistic adults, or those questioning their neurotype, in French-speaking Belgium, offering meetings and mutual aid to fill gaps in adult autism support.
initiatives.notes: Founding year not stated on the site. Listed in the Maison de l'Autisme Brussels directory alongside other Belgian autism organisations.

initiatives.name: Dr. Guislain Museum
initiatives.summary: Museum of the history of psychiatry and outsider art, housed in Belgium's oldest psychiatric hospital (inaugurated 1857) in Ghent, founded on the reform work of Dr. Joseph Guislain.
initiatives.notes: Exact year the museum (as opposed to the 1857 hospital) opened to the public could not be confirmed from primary sources; secondary sources vary (1980s). Run by the Guislain psychiatric institution/foundation, not by patients or an nd-led body.

initiatives.name: Kunsthuis Yellow Art
initiatives.summary: An art studio in Geel, Belgium for people with psychiatric or mental-health vulnerabilities, established as a permanent facility in 2004 by OPZ Geel, a public psychiatric care center; professional artists collaborate with about 30 participants outside a therapeutic framework.
initiatives.notes: Linked to OPZ Geel (public psychiatric hospital); grew out of the 2001 'Y.E.L.L.O.W.' exhibition curated by Jan Hoet. Serves psychiatric patients broadly, not a disability-specific studio.

initiatives.name: La "S" Grand Atelier
initiatives.summary: A center for art brut and contemporary art in Vielsalm, Belgium, founded in 1992 by director Anne-Francoise Rouche as a creative workshop for artists with intellectual disabilities, which also hosts professional artists for co-creation residencies.
initiatives.notes: Official site is live (HTTP 200) but currently shows only an 'under reconstruction' placeholder — facts sourced from BPS22's exhibition page and the Vielsalm tourism site instead. Recognized as a Centre d'Art Brut & Contemporain by the Wallonia-Brussels Federation in 2019.

initiatives.name: LAVA (Reading and Advisory Group of Adults with Autism)
initiatives.name_local: Lees- en Adviesgroep Volwassenen met Autisme
initiatives.summary: Ghent-based Flemish group of autistic adults that critically reviews autism research, advises on research priorities and media framing, and organises public lectures and reading salons on autism from a neurodiversity perspective.
initiatives.notes: Full member of EUCAP. States 'we are adults with autism'; partners with Leuven Autism Research and the Flemish Autism Action Plan.

initiatives.name: REV Belgium (Hearing Voices Network Belgium)
initiatives.name_local: Réseau sur l'Entente de Voix Belgique
initiatives.summary: French-speaking Belgian node of the international Hearing Voices Network, listed by Intervoice as the national contact for hearing-voices peer support in Belgium.
initiatives.notes: Listed on Intervoice's national-networks directory.

initiatives.name: Balkan Voices Network
initiatives.summary: A regional Hearing Voices network coordinating national representatives in Bosnia and Herzegovina (Tavan), Croatia (Dom Turnić), Serbia (Prostor) and Slovenia, running peer 'Art of Voices' training and an Erasmus+ Balkan Recovery College.
initiatives.region: Sarajevo (regional network spanning four countries; host city not stated)
initiatives.notes: Country field is an approximation: the network lists a Bosnian member (Tavan) first, but coordinates activity across Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Serbia and Slovenia. Affiliated with Intervoice.

initiatives.name: ABDA - Brazilian Attention Deficit Association
initiatives.name_local: Associação Brasileira do Déficit de Atenção (ABDA)
initiatives.summary: National patient association for ADHD, founded in Rio de Janeiro in 1999 and affiliated with the ADHD World Federation. Runs free monthly support groups in eight cities, trains health and education professionals, and helped shape Brazil's 2021 federal law on student health and education rights.
initiatives.region: Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro
initiatives.notes: Official domain tdah.org.br did not respond during verification (connection timeout from this network, DNS resolves fine); existence and current activity confirmed via its active YouTube channel and USP-hosted institutional materials referencing it.

initiatives.name: ABRACA - Brazilian Association for Action for the Rights of Autistic People
initiatives.name_local: Associação Brasileira para Ação por Direitos das Pessoas Autistas (ABRAÇA)
initiatives.summary: A national rights organization for autistic people, based in Fortaleza, Ceará. States it is led by autistic people and allied human-rights defenders, and works on self-advocacy, deinstitutionalization, and legal protections grounded in neurodiversity and the CRPD.
initiatives.notes: Founding year (2008) drawn from secondary coverage, not stated on the current site. Explicitly describes itself as 'protagonizada e liderada por pessoas autistas' (protagonized and led by autistic people).

initiatives.name: Acessa BH Festival
initiatives.summary: Belo Horizonte's annual disability-culture arts festival, in its sixth edition in 2026, curated by disabled curators Daniel and Lais Vitral under the principle 'nothing about us without us.' Programs dance, theatre, film, and literature across six venues, including neurodivergent artists.
initiatives.notes: Founding year inferred from '6th edition' in 2026, not directly confirmed. A broader disability-culture festival (physical, sensory, intellectual, and neurodivergent artists), not exclusively a neurodiversity event; included for its explicit disability-led curation model.

initiatives.name: Autistic Collective of UFRGS
initiatives.summary: Student collective at the Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul in Porto Alegre, founded in 2021 as part of the wave of autistic collectives inspired by USP's CAUSP. Provides a welcoming space and mutual support for autistic students, including those admitted through disability quotas.
initiatives.region: Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul
initiatives.notes: No independent website found; verified via UFRGS's own newspaper. Part of the CAUSP-inspired network of university autistic collectives; exact internal leadership composition not independently confirmed.

initiatives.name: Autistic Collective of USP (CAUSP)
initiatives.summary: Student collective at the University of São Paulo, founded in 2021 by an autistic undergraduate to support autistic students' retention in higher education. Runs peer mentoring, support groups, and awareness campaigns; inspired similar collectives at over 20 other Brazilian universities.
initiatives.notes: No independent website; operates via Instagram/Facebook (@coletivoautista). Founder Giulia Jardim Martinovic is autistic; collective won 2nd place in USP's 2021 Diversity Prize.

initiatives.name: Brazilian Autism Pride Movement (MOAB)
initiatives.summary: Founded in Brasília in 2005 by relatives of autistic people, one of Brazil's oldest national autism organizations. Runs the annual June 18 Autism Pride Day campaign and lobbies Congress on autism policy; family-led rather than a self-advocacy group.
initiatives.notes: Official domain moab.org.br no longer resolves; verified via Wikipedia, an active Instagram/Facebook presence (@moabbrasil), and Brazilian Congress recognition of its 10th anniversary.

initiatives.name: Brazilian Dyslexia Association (ABD)
initiatives.summary: Founded in São Paulo in 1983 by the father of a child with dyslexia. Offers technical guidance to dyslexic people, families, and educators, and lobbies for legislation and workplace access; one of Brazil's oldest learning-disability organizations.

initiatives.name: Cia. Teatral Ueinzz
initiatives.summary: Theatre company in São Paulo, founded around 1997, whose ensemble mixes users of mental health/psychiatric services with professional actors and philosophers, closely associated with philosopher Peter Pál Pelbart.
initiatives.notes: No dedicated official website found; sources vary on exact founding year (1996-1999). Confirmed active via a May 2024 performance listing. Peter Pál Pelbart is named as an actor-coordinator/member, not simply an outside academic observer. (original url https://x.com/ueinzz was a social-media link; replaced with source page)

initiatives.name: Hearing Voices Network - USP Ribeirão Preto
initiatives.summary: Hearing-voices peer information network based at the University of São Paulo's Ribeirão Preto campus, built jointly by voice-hearers and researchers at the Laboratory of Teaching and Research in Psychopathology, Drugs and Society. Shares coping strategies and hosts an in-person support group.
initiatives.notes: Founding year not stated. Site describes itself as built collaboratively by lived-experience voice-hearers and professional researchers, part of the international Hearing Voices Movement/Intervoice framework.

initiatives.name: Instituto ABCD
initiatives.summary: Nonprofit founded in São Paulo in 2009 by a family member of a person with dyslexia. Develops the free EduEdu learning app used by over a million students, trains teachers through its 'Todos Aprendem' program, and advocates for policy on dyslexia and other learning disorders.

initiatives.name: Introvertendo
initiatives.summary: Podcast and media outlet founded in Goiânia in 2018 by autistic students from the Federal University of Goiás, billed as Brazil's first podcast produced by autistic people. Paused in 2023 and relaunched in 2025 under production by NAIA Autismo with new hosts.
initiatives.notes: Site reachable (301 redirect to www subdomain, then 200). At least 80% of original-run guests were autistic; site includes audio description and Libras support.

initiatives.name: Mad in Brasil
initiatives.summary: Brazilian outlet of the international Mad in the World network, publishing critical-psychiatry journalism, lived-experience narratives, and mad-studies scholarship. Hosted at Fiocruz's National School of Public Health (ENSP) in Rio de Janeiro and runs a virtual library on psychiatric medication.
initiatives.region: Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro
initiatives.notes: Founding year not confirmed. Editorial leadership not disclosed in detail; publishes both academic/professional content and first-person accounts from psychiatric survivors.

initiatives.name: National Anti-Asylum Struggle Movement (MNLA)
initiatives.summary: National psychiatric-reform movement consolidated in 1993 at its first national meeting in Salvador, bringing together psychiatric-service users, family members, and mental-health workers. Campaigns against asylum-based care and organized May 18 as Brazil's National Anti-Asylum Struggle Day.
initiatives.notes: National movement with no fixed headquarters or independent website; located at the city of its founding national meeting (Salvador, 1993). Has an active Facebook page (mnlaemluta) that could not be verified via automated request from this network. Explicitly composed of 'usuários, familiares e trabalhadores' (users, family members, and workers).

initiatives.name: RIOSTOC
initiatives.name_local: Riostoc - Associação de familiares, amigos e pessoas com TOC e Síndrome de Tourette
initiatives.summary: Rio de Janeiro support association for people with OCD and Tourette syndrome and their families, coordinated by volunteer family members with input from mental-health professionals at UFRJ's IPUB and DPA. Holds free monthly online meetings and shares coping information.
initiatives.region: Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro
initiatives.notes: Founding year not stated on site. Explicitly coordinated by volunteer family members, advised by volunteer psychiatrists/psychologists; directs members to public healthcare rather than private practice.

initiatives.name: Specialisterne Brasil
initiatives.summary: São Paulo branch of the international Specialisterne network for autistic and neurodivergent employment. Trains autistic and neurodivergent jobseekers and places them with corporate clients including Itaú, IBM, and Carrefour, while advising companies on inclusive hiring and diversity training.
initiatives.notes: Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the Brazilian site; part of the international Specialisterne network founded in Denmark in 2004.

initiatives.name: UFSC Neurodivergent Students Project
initiatives.name_local: Neurodivergentes: vivências de estudantes autistas no ensino superior (UFSC)
initiatives.summary: University extension project at the Federal University of Santa Catarina in Florianópolis, coordinated by education professor Wellington Oliveira dos Santos. Runs recurring online sessions where autistic students and community members discuss higher-education experiences, employment, and identity.
initiatives.notes: Run as a recurring extension course (fourth edition as of February 2026); exact founding year and whether facilitators are themselves autistic are not stated in the source.

initiatives.name: Autism Today Association
initiatives.summary: A Bulgarian nonprofit founded in 2015, running four applied-behaviour-analysis therapy centres in Sofia, Pleven and Burgas for over 1,000 children a year, alongside training and policy-advocacy campaigns.
initiatives.notes: Established by ABA specialists, community members and parents. Primary activity is clinical ABA therapy delivery, which sits close to the ABA-provider category the brief flags for caution; kept because it also runs public-awareness and policy-advocacy work and is Bulgaria's Autism-Europe affiliated member. Flagged here for editorial review.

initiatives.name: Autistics 4 Autistics Ontario
initiatives.summary: Collective of autistic adults formed in 2017 that advocates for Ontario's autism policy and funding to shift from a charity model to a disability-rights model. An international affiliate of ASAN.
initiatives.notes: International affiliate of the Autistic Self Advocacy Network (ASAN).

initiatives.name: BC Hearing Voices Network
initiatives.summary: A Vancouver-based peer network supporting people who hear voices, see visions, or have other unique sensory experiences, listed by Intervoice as Canada's hearing-voices contact.

initiatives.name: Mad in Canada
initiatives.summary: Canadian affiliate of the Mad in the World network, publishing critical-psychiatry journalism, research summaries and lived-experience essays on science, psychiatry and social justice.
initiatives.region: Toronto, ON (national scope; editorial base not stated)
initiatives.notes: Part of the Mad in the World network (parent: Mad in America). Editorial team composition and founding year not stated on the site.

initiatives.name: Mad Pride Toronto
initiatives.summary: The organising collective behind Toronto's annual Mad Pride Week, tracing back to the 1993 'Psychiatric Survivor Pride Day', the founding event of the international Mad Pride movement.
initiatives.notes: Wikipedia identifies Toronto's Parkdale neighbourhood as the origin of the global Mad Pride movement, held annually except 1996.

initiatives.name: FUAN - Autism and Neurodiversity Union Foundation
initiatives.summary: A Chilean nonprofit combining autistic self-advocates and professionals that publishes public education on autism law, family mental health, and accessibility, and advocates on implementation of Chile's 2023 Autism Law.
initiatives.notes: Exact headquarters city not confirmed on the public site; documented activity centers on the Valparaíso region. President Gabriela Verdugo Weinberger; team includes Chantal Garay Soto, also president of FENAUT (Federación Nacional de Autismo).

initiatives.name: Mad Pride Chile (Orgullo Loco)
initiatives.summary: A psychiatric survivor movement, active since 2015, that organizes Chile's annual Mad Pride marches and campaigns against practices like electroshock, reclaiming madness as an identity rather than an illness.
initiatives.notes: Grew out of the Colectivo Autogestión Libre-Mente (founded 2014), a peer-support group of psychiatric service users/survivors meeting weekly at the Ailanto cultural center in Santiago. Instagram bio: 'Celebramos el derecho a la locura desde el año 2015'; also documented in academic literature.

initiatives.name: Millennium Nucleus on Disability and Citizenship (DISCA)
initiatives.summary: A Chilean state-funded interdisciplinary research center at Universidad Diego Portales studying disability and citizenship, using participatory methods with an advisory council of people with lived disability experience.
initiatives.notes: Scope is disability studies broadly (physical, sensory, intellectual, psychosocial), not neurodiversity-exclusive, but includes research on psychiatric institutionalization and disabled youth activism. ANID-funded Millennium Nucleus, director Florencia Herrera.

initiatives.name: Beijing Stars and Rain Education Institute for Autism
initiatives.summary: China's first NGO dedicated to autistic children, founded in Beijing in 1993 by a parent, running an autism education and training programme for children and parents.
initiatives.notes: Site intermittently unreachable, verified via Wikipedia/British Council. Older autismchina.org domain is now dead.

initiatives.name: AUTISCOL (Colombian Autistic People's Association)
initiatives.summary: A Colombian association made up of adult autistic people that publishes self-advocacy writing on rights and neurodiversity, tracks pending autism-related legislation, and runs public petitions and reports.
initiatives.notes: Explicitly self-describes as run by autistic people ('conformada por un grupo de autistas'). Also active on Substack (autiscol.substack.com) and Instagram (@autiscol). No fixed city/office found; coordinates approximate Bogotá as a placeholder for a national, largely online organization.

initiatives.name: DISFAM Colombia
initiatives.summary: The Colombian chapter of the international dyslexia/specific-learning-differences network DISFAM, doing advocacy and outreach for families and professionals and pushing regulation of Colombia's 2022 dyslexia law.
initiatives.notes: Run by named regional representatives (Bogotá, Cali), not self-described as dyslexic-led. Most recent dated content is a December 2024 legislative working meeting on Colombia's dyslexia decree.

initiatives.name: BarrileTEA
initiatives.summary: San José nonprofit founded in November 2018 that campaigns for autism rights and legislation in Costa Rica. Known for its annual kite-flying 'BarrileTEAda' awareness events and its advocacy role in Costa Rica's 2021 Autism Law and 2024 implementing regulation.
initiatives.notes: Official site barriletea.org was intermittently unresolvable on repeated checks, so the confirmed-live Facebook page is used as the primary url, with a 2024 elmundo.cr news article as source_url. Founder Jessica Varela's own neurodivergent status was not stated in available sources, so leadership is marked unknown rather than assumed.

initiatives.name: Croatian Union of Associations for Autism (SUZAH)
initiatives.summary: A Zagreb-based umbrella body coordinating 13 Croatian autism associations, tracing its roots to a 1979 parent group, running a helpline and advisory service and advocating for autistic people and families nationally.
initiatives.notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Founding traced to the first Croatian parents-of-autistic-children group in 1979; current internal leadership composition not detailed on the site.

initiatives.name: Autism Support Famagusta
initiatives.summary: A Cypriot charity founded by parents and friends of autistic people near Famagusta, running a Summer Club since 2014, outreach and parent coffee mornings, and teacher-training seminars.
initiatives.notes: Autism-Europe affiliated member; participates in the Pan Cypriot Autism Support Committee. Founding year not stated, though its Summer Club has run since 2014.

initiatives.name: Adventor (A-komunita)
initiatives.summary: Prague community centre and self-help organisation for autistic children, teenagers and adults, running individualised support, an antiquarian bookshop, and inclusion projects with mixed autistic and non-autistic teams.
initiatives.notes: Runs the KC Kopec community centre. Full member of EUCAP. Site blocks bare curl requests (403) but is reachable with a browser user agent and was read in full via fetch.

initiatives.name: Akrasia (Association for Adults with ADHD)
initiatives.name_local: Spolek pro dospělé s diagnózou ADHD
initiatives.summary: Czech association founded in 2022 by psychologists, some with personal ADHD experience, running a nationwide network of peer support groups, workshops and an online resource-navigation tool for adults with ADHD.
initiatives.notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations. Also active in Brno and Pardubice.

initiatives.name: European Council of Autistic People (EUCAP)
initiatives.summary: An umbrella network of autistic-led organisations from across Europe that lobbies EU and national institutions, coordinates member groups, and represents autistic people in disability policy forums.
initiatives.notes: Registered as 'European Council of Autistic People z.s.' in Prague, but is a pan-European body: 27 member organisations across 18 countries as of the source page. Prague is a legal registration address, not an operational hub; board and members are distributed across Europe.

initiatives.name: Hearing Voices Network Czech Republic
initiatives.summary: The Czech national node of the international Hearing Voices Network, listed by Intervoice as the Czech Republic's hearing-voices contact.

initiatives.name: NAUTIS (National Institute for Autism)
initiatives.summary: A Prague-based Czech national institute providing free counselling, diagnosis, therapy and training on autism, and running the AutismPort information portal, funded partly by EU and Czech government grants.
initiatives.notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Grew out of APLA Praha, the organisation that founded the Pasparta publishing social enterprise; exact founding year not stated on the current site.

initiatives.name: PASPARTA
initiatives.summary: A Czech publishing house and social enterprise, founded by the autism organisation APLA Praha, that creates adapted graphic-design and publishing jobs for people with autism.
initiatives.notes: Founded December 2012 by APLA Praha (now part of NAUTIS); publishes psychology, autism and special-education titles and offers graphic design services, employing people with autism in adapted roles. Cited as a good-practice example at the UN.

initiatives.name: Autisme Ungdom
initiatives.summary: Danish youth and disability organisation for autistic people aged 13-35, founded 2019 with a board composed entirely of young autistic people, running six regional chapters, a Discord community, and an annual summer camp.
initiatives.notes: Associate member of EUCAP; found while cross-checking the EUCAP member list. Membership does not require a formal diagnosis.

initiatives.name: Autisme- og Aspergerforeningen
initiatives.summary: Danish national association describing itself as 'autisternes egen forening' (autistic people's own association), running local meeting places across the country, an annual Aukon conference, and disability-policy advocacy.
initiatives.notes: Full member of EUCAP. No fixed single office; placed at a central Denmark coordinate. Automated curl checks returned a non-standard 454 status from this network; content was independently confirmed via fetch.

initiatives.name: Hearing Voices Network Denmark
initiatives.summary: Denmark's national Hearing Voices Network, listed by Intervoice, offering peer information and groups for voice-hearers.

initiatives.name: Mad in Denmark
initiatives.summary: Danish affiliate of the Mad in the World network, launched around 2023, publishing critical-psychiatry articles and lived-experience accounts in Danish and English.
initiatives.region: Copenhagen (national scope; editorial base not stated)
initiatives.notes: Part of the Mad in the World network. Launch year drawn from a Mad in the UK announcement post, not the site itself.

initiatives.name: Ordblindeforeningen i Danmark
initiatives.summary: Danish dyslexia association based in Taastrup, giving free professional guidance to individuals, schools and employers, running regional and youth chapters, and publishing a member magazine on dyslexia.
initiatives.notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Patron since 2024 is Princess Marie of Denmark.

initiatives.name: Specialisterne Foundation
initiatives.summary: A Danish foundation, founded by the father of an autistic son, that places autistic and other neurodivergent people into paid jobs with partner companies through an assessment and training model.
initiatives.notes: Founded by Thorkil Sonne; credited with creating roughly 10,000 jobs for autistic people globally through corporate partnerships (SAP, Microsoft, IBM and others). Included as a large, well-known anchor organisation; leadership is not itself predominantly neurodivergent-led.

initiatives.name: World Network of Users and Survivors of Psychiatry (WNUSP)
initiatives.summary: An international organisation of psychiatric survivors, founded in 1991 (as the World Federation of Psychiatric Users, renamed WNUSP in 1997), advocating for the rights of people labelled with mental illness within the UN human-rights system.
initiatives.notes: Official domain wnusp.net is unreachable (connection refused) and wnusp.org now resolves to an unrelated retail site, so Wikipedia is used as both url and source_url. Wikipedia states WNUSP is based in Odense, Denmark since 2000 and is explicitly led by survivors of psychiatry.

initiatives.name: Dominican Autism Foundation
initiatives.summary: Santo Domingo nonprofit founded in 1999 and made up of parents of autistic children. Provides autism awareness education, a professional training diploma in neurodevelopmental-disorder evaluation, and support services for families.
initiatives.notes: Site lists training sessions scheduled into 2026, indicating current activity; returns HTTP 406 to bare requests without browser headers (bot-filtering quirk, not a dead site). Membership explicitly described as the children's own parents, hence ally-led rather than nd-led.

initiatives.name: Estonian Autism Alliance
initiatives.summary: An umbrella organisation based in Tartu coordinating regional autism associations across Estonia, providing training and counselling to network members and advocating for autistic people's rights.
initiatives.notes: Autism-Europe affiliated member. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

initiatives.name: MTÜ Autistid
initiatives.summary: Estonian association, established 2019 as the Estonian Autistic Women's Association, that spreads information about autism and neurodiversity, builds community, and advocates to improve conditions for autistic people in Estonia.
initiatives.notes: Full member of EUCAP, formerly Eesti Autistlike Naiste Ühing (Estonian Autistic Women's Association), founded 8 March 2019. Site notes it is under renovation. The EUCAP-listed URL (eany.ee) redirects to autistid.ee, used here. Leadership not explicitly stated on-site as autistic-led, so marked unknown despite the association's name and history.

initiatives.name: Association of Different Learners (FINDER)
initiatives.summary: Helsinki-based Finnish association supporting people with dyslexia, dyscalculia and other learning difficulties in work and education, offering counselling, peer 'experience expert' activities and policy advocacy.
initiatives.notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association.

initiatives.name: Autism Foundation Finland
initiatives.summary: A Helsinki-based Finnish foundation and KELA-approved service provider offering guidance, employment and education support, and 24-hour residential and supported housing for autistic people nationwide.
initiatives.notes: Listed as an Autism-Europe affiliated member, distinct from the full-member Finnish Association for Autism and Asperger's Syndrome. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

initiatives.name: Finnish Association for Autism and Asperger's Syndrome
initiatives.summary: Finland's national autism federation, coordinating member associations, publishing the quarterly Autismi-lehti magazine, and providing peer support, counselling and professional training nationwide.
initiatives.notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

initiatives.name: Mad in Finland
initiatives.summary: Finnish affiliate of the Mad in the World network, publishing critical mental-health journalism, event listings and a media-monitoring digest in Finnish.
initiatives.region: Helsinki (national scope; editorial base not stated)
initiatives.notes: Part of the Mad in the World network.

initiatives.name: Suomen Autismikirjon Yhdistys (ASY)
initiatives.summary: Helsinki-based Finnish association working for the wellbeing and equality of autistic people, running peer support groups, an autism-friendly certification programme, and summer and autumn community gatherings.
initiatives.notes: Full member of EUCAP. Leadership composition not explicitly stated as autistic-led on the pages read, so marked unknown despite EUCAP full-member status.

initiatives.name: Suomen Moniääniset (Finnish Hearing Voices Network)
initiatives.summary: Finland's national hearing-voices association, providing support to voice-hearers and their families and listed as Finland's Intervoice contact.
initiatives.notes: Registered association ('ry').

initiatives.name: CLE Autistes
initiatives.name_local: Collectif pour la Liberté d'Expression des Autistes
initiatives.summary: A French self-advocacy collective, run entirely by autistic people, that organises peer support, training and campaigns and treats autism as a political identity rather than only a diagnosis.
initiatives.notes: Founded September 2018; over 130 members and 400 supporters nationally. Governed by a collegial leadership composed entirely of autistic people, renewed by co-optation.

initiatives.name: Compagnie de l'Oiseau-Mouche
initiatives.summary: Roubaix theatre company founded in 1978 (professionalized 1981) as France's first artistic ESAT, with a permanent troupe of actors with intellectual/psychological disability directed by rotating outside stage directors.
initiatives.notes: General/artistic direction held by non-disabled staff; productions staged by guest directors. Permanent troupe of ~20-23 comédien·ne·s have intellectual/psychological disability.

initiatives.name: French Federation of Dys Disorders (FFDys)
initiatives.summary: French federation of regional associations for people with dyslexia, dyspraxia, dyscalculia and related developmental disorders, running an annual National Dys Day and professional training programme.
initiatives.notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Its 20th National Dys Day fell in 2026. Site describes mobilising 'parents and professionals throughout France,' hence marked ally-led.

initiatives.name: REV France (Hearing Voices Network France)
initiatives.name_local: Réseau français sur l'Entente de Voix
initiatives.summary: France's national Hearing Voices Network, coordinating peer support groups for voice-hearers and listed as France's Intervoice contact.

initiatives.name: Aspies e.V.
initiatives.summary: The oldest and largest German self-help association for autistic adults, run by an all-autistic board, offering local peer groups nationwide, a crisis helpline and an online self-help forum.
initiatives.notes: Around 550 members, board of five autistic people, registered at Berlin-Charlottenburg district court. Member of EUCAP. Automated HTTPS checks from this session failed with a TLS renegotiation error against aspies.de specifically; live page content was independently confirmed via a fetch tool, so it is not treated as down.

initiatives.name: Atelier Goldstein
initiatives.summary: An artist studio in Frankfurt, Germany, founded in 2001 as a project of Lebenshilfe Frankfurt, offering individual artistic assistance from professional artists to people with cognitive disabilities; work has shown at documenta fifteen and Schirn Kunsthalle.
initiatives.notes: Site's WAF returns HTTP 500 on plain HEAD requests but 200 on GET (verified live via GET and WebFetch).

initiatives.name: Autismus-Kultur
initiatives.summary: German website written from an autistic perspective on how autistic people can live well in a non-autistic world, offering practical guidance, tips and community discussion rather than clinical advice.
initiatives.notes: Site self-describes as written from an autistic perspective. Returns 403 to automated fetches (bot-blocking); reachable and returns 200 to a plain curl with a browser user agent. No stated headquarters city; placed at a geographic-centre-of-Germany coordinate as a placeholder.

initiatives.name: autSocial e.V.
initiatives.summary: Hamburg-based German association run under the motto 'von Autist*innen für Autist*innen' (by autistic people for autistic people), operating self-help groups, online workshops on masking and workplace inclusion, and creative projects like autArt.
initiatives.notes: Full member of EUCAP; funded in part through Hamburg's social affairs authority.

initiatives.name: Federal Association for Dyslexia and Dyscalculia (BVL)
initiatives.summary: German federal association, established around 1976, advocating for accommodations for people with dyslexia and dyscalculia in school, training and careers, with regional chapters and a therapist certification programme.
initiatives.notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Founding year inferred from the site's own '50 years' anniversary claim.

initiatives.name: Kunstwerkstatt der Lebenshilfe Berlin
initiatives.summary: An inclusive art workshop run by Lebenshilfe Berlin in Berlin, Germany, active since at least 1999 (its first exhibition), where professional facilitators guide clients with intellectual disabilities in painting and other visual art.
initiatives.notes: Domain works reliably only over plain HTTP; HTTPS fails TLS handshake. Exact founding year not stated on-site — earliest documented activity is its 1999 exhibition.

initiatives.name: Mad in Germany
initiatives.summary: German affiliate of the Mad in the World network, publishing critical-psychiatry essays, translated international pieces and lived-experience accounts in German.
initiatives.region: Berlin (national scope; editorial base not stated)
initiatives.notes: Part of the Mad in the World network.

initiatives.name: Netzwerk Stimmenhören (German Hearing Voices Network)
initiatives.summary: Germany's national Hearing Voices Network association, coordinating peer groups and information on hearing voices, listed as Germany's Intervoice contact.
initiatives.notes: Registered association ('e.V.'). Old domain netzwerk-stimmenhoeren.de now redirects here.

initiatives.name: Prinzhorn Collection
initiatives.summary: Collection of art by psychiatric patients assembled by Hans Prinzhorn at Heidelberg University's psychiatric clinic from 1919, with a dedicated museum inaugurated in 2001; now ~40,000 works from 1825 to today.
initiatives.notes: Part of Heidelberg University Hospital; a research/curatorial institution, not patient- or artist-run.

initiatives.name: Theater Thikwa
initiatives.summary: Berlin theatre company founded in 1991, self-described as a company where artists 'with and without disability' make theatre together; artistic direction is currently shared by Nicole Hummel and Laura Besch.

initiatives.name: Autism Awareness Care and Training Centre (AACT)
initiatives.summary: Accra-based centre for autistic children founded in 1998 by a nurse practitioner and parent, providing behaviour management, therapy, and individualized education plans.
initiatives.notes: Parent-led, professionally run. Site returns 406 to a bare curl user agent; needs a full browser-style header.

initiatives.name: Greek Society for the Protection of Autistic People (GSPAP)
initiatives.summary: Founded in Athens in November 1992 by 80 parents of autistic people from Athens, Piraeus and Crete, this national society runs residential and day-centre services in Attica, Macedonia and Ioannina.
initiatives.notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Explicitly parent-founded; current governance not detailed on the site.

initiatives.name: Hearing Voices Network Greece
initiatives.summary: Greece's national Hearing Voices Network, offering peer information and groups for voice-hearers and listed as Greece's Intervoice contact.

initiatives.name: Mad in Greece
initiatives.summary: Greek affiliate of the Mad in the World network, run by a volunteer contributor team publishing psychopharmaceutical-policy critique, personal narratives and art on psychiatric experience.
initiatives.region: Athens (national scope; editorial base not stated)
initiatives.notes: Site names a volunteer team page ('Our Team') and invites contributions; individual members' lived-experience status not confirmed, hence 'mixed' rather than 'nd-led'.

initiatives.name: NeuroDiversity Association Hong Kong (NDAHK)
initiatives.summary: Hong Kong advocacy organisation, established in 2024, promoting the value of neurodiversity through cross-sector partnerships, education, and conferences.

initiatives.name: Hungarian Autistic Society (AOSZ)
initiatives.summary: Hungary's national autism federation, based in Budapest, listed as a full member of Autism-Europe representing autistic people and their families in national advocacy.
initiatives.notes: The live site is currently a bare landing page with no navigable content, so facts are drawn from Autism-Europe's official August 2026 member directory rather than the org's own site. Founding year and leadership composition unconfirmed.

initiatives.name: Mars Foundation
initiatives.summary: A Budapest foundation for autism awareness offering family and professional training, downloadable social-story resources, a parent support club, and urban life-skills training for autistic teenagers.
initiatives.notes: Listed as an Autism-Europe affiliated member. Runs Erasmus+ international projects; founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

initiatives.name: Einhverfusamtökin (Icelandic Autism Association)
initiatives.summary: Iceland's national autism association, based in Reykjavik, providing autism education resources, rights and benefits information, and social groups for autistic youth and adults in Reykjavik and Akureyri.
initiatives.notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

initiatives.name: Hugarafl
initiatives.summary: A Reykjavik peer-run mental-health community offering recovery, empowerment and hearing-voices support groups run by and for its members; Iceland's Intervoice contact.
initiatives.notes: Site describes itself as 'samfélag jafningja sem styðja hvert annað' (a community of peers who support one another); broader peer mental-health community whose activities include the Icelandic hearing-voices group.

initiatives.name: Action for Autism (AFA) - National Centre for Autism
initiatives.summary: Delhi-based Indian non-profit, founded in 1991 as a parent support group, running assessment, education, therapy, employment, and self-advocacy services for autistic people.
initiatives.notes: Runs a Self-Advocacy Programme, but it is professionally facilitated rather than self-advocate-run.

initiatives.name: Bapu Trust for Research on Mind & Discourse
initiatives.summary: Pune-based trust doing non-coercive, community-based mental health work, including an urban community mental health and inclusion programme; founder was active in the international Hearing Voices movement.
initiatives.notes: About page 404'd during verification; leadership framing not explicitly self-declared. Site returns 406 to a bare curl user agent.

initiatives.name: Mad in South Asia
initiatives.summary: Regional affiliate of the Mad in the World network covering India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Bhutan and Nepal, run by a core team of therapists, researchers, professors and psychiatric-service users who center survivors' own accounts.
initiatives.region: Pune, Maharashtra (approximate anchor; site states no single national HQ)
initiatives.notes: Regional, not single-country; India used only as an approximate map anchor given the site's connections to Pune-based Bapu Trust and lack of a stated HQ city. Site explicitly states service users/survivors are kept 'first' among contributors.

initiatives.name: TCI Global (Transforming Communities for Inclusion)
initiatives.summary: A global federation of organisations of persons with psychosocial disabilities, grown since 2012 from an Asia-Pacific network supported by Pune's Bapu Trust and the International Disability Alliance, campaigning to abolish coercive mental-health law.
initiatives.region: Pune, Maharashtra (originating hub; now a global federation)
initiatives.notes: Explicitly self-describes as 'a global Organisation of persons with psychosocial disabilities [an OPD]'. Originated as the 'TransAsian strategy group' (2012-2014) working with Bapu Trust, already in the atlas. The domain tci-asia.org, once its Asia-Pacific site, now resolves to an unrelated gambling site and should not be used.

initiatives.name: Ummeed Child Development Center
initiatives.summary: Mumbai-based non-profit founded in 2001 by a developmental pediatrician, providing trans-disciplinary clinical services, training, and research for children with developmental disabilities.

initiatives.name: Yayasan MPATI (Masyarakat Peduli Autis Indonesia)
initiatives.summary: Indonesian national foundation, evolved from a 1998 parent community, focused on training and empowering parents of autistic children and advocating for government autism support policy.
initiatives.notes: Evolved from KOMPAA (Komunitas Peduli Autis dan ADHD), founded in 1998.

initiatives.name: AsIAm
initiatives.summary: Ireland's national autism charity, founded in 2014 by autistic CEO Adam Harris, working on autism-friendly community certification, policy and self-advocacy, with a stated policy of at least half its board being autistic.
initiatives.notes: Registered as a Disabled Persons' Organisation; runs the Autism Friendly Towns programme.

initiatives.name: Dyslexia Ireland
initiatives.summary: Dublin-based Irish charity providing dyslexia and dyscalculia assessments, tutoring, training for parents and teachers, and policy advocacy, funded in part by the Department of Education.
initiatives.notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Site returns 403 to some automated fetch tools (bot-blocking) but was read in full via a different fetch and confirmed live with a browser-header curl.

initiatives.name: Hearing Voices Network Ireland
initiatives.summary: Ireland's national Hearing Voices Network, coordinating local peer groups and training, historically linked to academics Harry Gijbels and Lydia Sapouna at University College Cork.
initiatives.notes: Distinct from the editorial site Mad in Ireland (madinireland.com), already in the atlas; both trace to the same UCC-linked circle of academics and voice-hearers.

initiatives.name: Mad in Ireland
initiatives.summary: An Irish collective of psychiatric survivors, peer workers, academics and practitioners that publishes critical commentary and organises events challenging the dominant diagnostic model in mental health care.
initiatives.notes: An affiliate of the international Mad in the World network. Governing team includes psychiatric survivors/peer support leaders alongside mental health practitioners and academics.

initiatives.name: Beit Issie Shapiro
initiatives.summary: Israeli nonprofit that develops, researches, and scales disability service models such as early intervention and assistive technology, and shares them internationally.
initiatives.notes: Holds UN ECOSOC consultative status.

initiatives.name: Bizchut - The Israel Human Rights Center for People with Disabilities
initiatives.summary: Independent legal-advocacy and watchdog organisation advancing the rights of people with all disability types in Israel through litigation, policy work, and a public inquiries hotline.
initiatives.notes: Cross-disability, not neurodiversity-specific; board combines disabled people, parents, professionals, and academics.

initiatives.name: Shutaf Inclusion Programs
initiatives.summary: Jerusalem-based "reverse inclusion" nonprofit running year-round camps and youth-leadership programs where disabled and non-disabled children and teens participate together.
initiatives.notes: Direct page fetch was blocked by a bot filter; verified live via curl (200 OK) and secondary sources.

initiatives.name: ARCI Intervoice Italia
initiatives.name_local: ARCI Intervoice Italia APS (formerly Rete Italiana Noi e le Voci)
initiatives.summary: Italy's national Hearing Voices association, offering information and peer exchange for voice-hearers, professionals and relatives, treating hearing voices as a human experience rather than a symptom.
initiatives.region: Italy (national association; HQ city not stated)
initiatives.notes: Rebranded from 'Rete Italiana Noi e le Voci' (parlaconlevoci.it, now a redirect page) to ARCI Intervoice Italia APS. Registered as an Italian APS (Associazione di Promozione Sociale).

initiatives.name: Aspergeronline
initiatives.summary: An Italian association founded by an autistic designer that offers self-screening tools, peer community, a podcast and resources for autistic people and professionals, built with an autistic development team.
initiatives.notes: Founded January 2023 by Simone Favarin, an autistic designer and communicator; became a formal association (ETS) in December 2023. Reports 356,817 unique users and 60,000+ RAADS-R screenings completed in 2024.

initiatives.name: Italian Dyslexia Association (AID)
initiatives.summary: Bologna-based Italian association, founded 1997, supporting people with specific learning disorders across their lifespan through teacher and family training, the LibroAID digital textbook platform, and school/workplace advocacy.
initiatives.notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association.

initiatives.name: Mad in Italy
initiatives.summary: Italian affiliate of the Mad in the World network, founded in 2018 and run by a mixed board of a psychiatrist, a pharmacology researcher and two psychiatric-survivor advocates.
initiatives.region: Rome (national scope; editorial base not stated)
initiatives.notes: Board includes Susanna Brunelli and Cristina Paderi, both self-described psychiatric-survivor advocates, alongside a psychiatrist and a pharmacology researcher.

initiatives.name: Neuropeculiar
initiatives.summary: Italian association founded and directed by autistic people that campaigns for self-representation and self-determination under a neurodiversity and Disability Studies framework, and organises the annual AUTcamp gathering.
initiatives.notes: Full member of EUCAP. No single stated headquarters; located at Rome, where its 2026 AUTcamp event is held.

initiatives.name: Able Art Japan
initiatives.name_local: エイブル・アート・ジャパン
initiatives.summary: Able Art Japan is a Tokyo NPO founded in 1995 that supports people with disabilities in creating, exhibiting, and selling art; it co-founded the affiliated Able Art Company (2007), an agency licensing disabled artists' work commercially.
initiatives.notes: Related entity Able Art Company (https://ableartcom.jp/, curl 200 OK) is an artist agency founded 2007 by three Japanese NPOs including Able Art Japan, HQ in Nara with a Tokyo office. Neither site explicitly claims artist-led governance; language is 'together with people with disabilities.'

initiatives.name: Atelier Incurve
initiatives.summary: Atelier Incurve (renamed INCURVE in April 2024) is a licensed day-service art facility in Osaka operated by the Social Welfare Corporation Sou-kai for adults with intellectual disabilities under Japan's disability-support law.
initiatives.notes: Site confirms operation by Social Welfare Corporation Sou-kai and the 2024 rename to INCURVE, but does not state the studio's original founding year on pages checked.

initiatives.name: Japan Developmental Disabilities Network (JDDnet)
initiatives.name_local: 日本発達障害ネットワーク
initiatives.summary: Tokyo-based umbrella network of about 57 affiliated parent groups, academic societies, and professional bodies covering autism, ADHD, and learning disabilities nationally in Japan.
initiatives.notes: Founded following Japan's 2004 Developmental Disabilities Support Law.

initiatives.name: Urakawa Bethel House
initiatives.summary: Social welfare corporation in Hokkaido founded in 1984 by former psychiatric patients and a social worker, practicing "Tojisha-Kenkyu" (self-directed peer research) into members' own psychiatric experiences.
initiatives.notes: Explicitly by-and-for psychiatric survivors (tojisha); runs an annual 'Bethel Festival' and cooperative small businesses.

initiatives.name: ADHD Jersey
initiatives.summary: Jersey (Channel Islands) not-for-profit combining lived ADHD experience with professional expertise, running adult and youth ADHD support programmes, awareness talks and a community hub in St Helier.
initiatives.notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations. Site states it was 'built by people who truly understand ADHD because we've lived it,' combined with professional expertise.

initiatives.name: Latvian Autism Association
initiatives.summary: A Riga-based association founded on 1 October 2006 to protect the rights and interests of autistic people in Latvia, running a psychosocial rehabilitation programme for children and joining Autism-Europe in 2013.
initiatives.notes: Listed as an Autism-Europe affiliated member (joined 2013). Chaired by Līga Bērziņa as of the source page; leadership composition (parent-led vs. self-advocate) not explicitly stated.

initiatives.name: Lebanese Autism Society (LAS)
initiatives.summary: Beirut-based membership NGO founded by parents and professionals, running educational, vocational, and consultancy programs for autistic children and teens.
initiatives.notes: Runs a Technical School for Adolescents with Autism.

initiatives.name: Rain Children
initiatives.summary: A Vilnius-based Lithuanian nonprofit uniting families of autistic children, autistic adults and professionals, running a resource directory, peer-support groups for autistic youth, and a community handmade-goods shop.
initiatives.notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Site references '10 years' of operation without giving an exact founding date; unites families, adults with autism, and professionals rather than being purely parent-led.

initiatives.name: Fondation Autisme Luxembourg (FAL)
initiatives.summary: A Luxembourg foundation, marking its 30th anniversary in 2026, providing residential care at five sites for 39 autistic residents, family support to about 650 families, and professional training on autism.
initiatives.notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Founding year (1996) inferred from a 30th-anniversary reference on the site in 2026.

initiatives.name: National Autism Society of Malaysia (NASOM)
initiatives.summary: Malaysia's longest-running national autism body, founded in 1986, running early intervention, therapy, vocational training, and residential independent-living programmes nationwide.

initiatives.name: Autism Parents Association (APA)
initiatives.summary: A Maltese voluntary organisation of over 450 member families of autistic children, running a private peer-support network, an autism handbook, seminars, and the SIPT sensory-integration youth programme.
initiatives.notes: Full member of Autism-Europe, registered as voluntary organisation VO802. Founded by parents of autistic children; founding year not stated on the site.

initiatives.name: Hearing Voices Network Malta
initiatives.summary: Malta's national Hearing Voices peer group, listed by Intervoice as the country's national contact for hearing-voices support.
initiatives.notes: Only public presence is this Wix site; no separate domain found.

initiatives.name: Autistas de México
initiatives.summary: Mexico City organization that describes itself as the first association in Mexico created by and for autistic people. Offers autism/ADHD differential diagnosis, therapy and coaching delivered by autistic staff, plus community support groups, reaching clients nationwide online.
initiatives.notes: Self-description confirmed verbatim on site: 'la primera asociación en México creada por y para autistas.' Also participates in the Marcha del Orgullo Loco. Founding year not stated precisely, left null rather than guessed. Charges for clinical/diagnostic services alongside its community/advocacy work.

initiatives.name: Colectivo Chuhcan
initiatives.summary: Mexico City civil association founded in 2011 and run entirely by people with lived experience of psychiatric diagnosis. Provides peer support, human-rights advocacy against forced institutionalization, and helped organize Mexico's first Mad Pride march.
initiatives.notes: No independent Chuhcan website or confirmed social-media handle was found; url/source_url point to a Mad in Mexico interview with founder Raúl Montoya. Also active in Red Orgullo Loco México's annual Marcha del Orgullo Loco alongside other user-led collectives (SinColectivo, Colectiva Meteorita) that could not be independently verified.

initiatives.name: SOS Autism Moldova
initiatives.summary: A Chișinău-based Moldovan association founded in May 2008 by parents of autistic children, offering ABA, speech and art therapy, and acting as the main advocate to national authorities on autism policy.
initiatives.notes: Autism-Europe affiliated member. Explicitly founded by a group of parents of autistic children.

initiatives.name: Atelier Herenplaats
initiatives.summary: An art studio and gallery in Rotterdam, Netherlands, founded in 1991, providing studio space and training for about 35 artists with intellectual disabilities or psychiatric backgrounds, supervised by professional artists and art teachers.

initiatives.name: Autminds
initiatives.summary: Dutch congress for and by autistic people, run for eleven years out of Delft, bringing autistic adults together for talks, workshops and networking; its final edition is scheduled for October 2026.
initiatives.notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Founding year inferred from the site's own '11 years' claim ahead of its announced final October 2026 congress; included despite the planned wind-down because it is still active as of verification.

initiatives.name: European Network of (Ex-)Users and Survivors of Psychiatry (ENUSP)
initiatives.summary: A grassroots umbrella organisation, founded in 1990 by Dutch psychiatric survivors, uniting national and local user/survivor organisations across Europe to advocate directly on human rights in mental health.
initiatives.region: Netherlands (founding country; no fixed current HQ stated)
initiatives.notes: Site states: 'We directly represent the views of people who are or have been on the receiving end of psychiatric services' and describes itself as the only grassroots umbrella working across Europe on this basis. No current registered-office city found; located here at its 1990 founding country only.

initiatives.name: Mad in the Netherlands
initiatives.summary: Dutch affiliate of the Mad in the World network, launched 1 February 2022 as the tenth national affiliate, making international critical-psychiatry and psychopharmacology knowledge accessible in Dutch.
initiatives.region: Amsterdam (national scope; editorial base not stated)
initiatives.notes: Part of the Mad in the World network.

initiatives.name: PAS Nederland
initiatives.summary: A Dutch peer-run association for people with autism and average-to-high intelligence, mostly staffed by autistic board members and volunteers, running local groups in several Dutch cities.
initiatives.notes: Activities run in multiple cities including Alkmaar, Utrecht, Nijmegen, Weert, 's-Hertogenbosch, Leiden and Zwolle; The Hague used as the organisation's registered base.

initiatives.name: Stichting Weerklank
initiatives.summary: The Dutch national Hearing Voices foundation, supporting people who hear voices, see visions or have other unusual perceptions, and their relatives, and listed as the Netherlands' Intervoice contact.

initiatives.name: Altogether Autism
initiatives.summary: Free, government-funded nationwide autism information and advisory service for autistic people, whanau, and professionals in New Zealand.
initiatives.notes: Run in partnership between Your Way | Kia Roha and Parent to Parent New Zealand; includes an autistic-led peer offshoot, 'By Autistics for Autistics'.

initiatives.name: Autism New Zealand
initiatives.summary: National New Zealand charity supporting autistic people and their families through a Board of Trustees and nationwide services.
initiatives.notes: At least one board member is autistic and also a parent of an autistic adult; overall composition reads as ally-led/mixed.

initiatives.name: Hearing Voices Network Aotearoa New Zealand
initiatives.summary: New Zealand's national Hearing Voices Network, providing information and peer group support for voice-hearers and listed as the country's Intervoice contact.

initiatives.name: Patrick Speech and Languages Centre (PSLC)
initiatives.summary: Nigeria's first dedicated autism centre, opened in Lagos in 2006, offering speech and language therapy, vocational training, and a professional training academy.
initiatives.notes: Parent-founded, professionally run; operates two centres in Ikeja and Lekki.

initiatives.name: Autismenyheter
initiatives.summary: A Norwegian-language news and commentary site about autism, written by a single autistic author from a neurodiversity perspective, covering research and autistic first-person experience.
initiatives.notes: Run by a single autistic author who publishes under the name 'Soda' and lives on an island near Bergen; launched 3 June 2018 to fill a gap in Norwegian-language autism coverage.

initiatives.name: Mad in Norway
initiatives.summary: Norwegian affiliate of the Mad in the World network, launched in 2019 under editor-in-chief Birgit Valla, publishing critical-psychiatry commentary and research.
initiatives.region: Oslo (national scope; editorial base not stated)
initiatives.notes: Editor-in-chief Birgit Valla is a psychologist by training; site does not state the outlet is survivor-led, hence leadership marked unknown rather than assumed.

initiatives.name: Autism Society of Pakistan (ASP)
initiatives.summary: National umbrella non-profit registered in 2010, running Autism Resource Centres in Rawalpindi and Islamabad offering diagnosis, therapy, school-integration support, and parent training.
initiatives.notes: Board of Governors composed of professionals and affected parents. Site returns 403 to a bare curl user agent; resolves 200 with full browser headers.

initiatives.name: Karachi Down Syndrome Program (KDSP)
initiatives.summary: Karachi-founded nonprofit, registered in 2014, delivering family support, healthcare, education, and skills programmes for people with Down syndrome, with chapters in four other Pakistani cities.
initiatives.notes: Registered as a Section 42 nonprofit company; also runs chapters in Faisalabad, Islamabad, Hyderabad, and North Nazimabad.

initiatives.name: ASO TEA Paraguay
initiatives.name_local: Asociación de Padres y/o Tutores de Personas con Trastorno del Espectro Autista (ASO TEA)
initiatives.summary: A Paraguayan parent-and-guardian association for people with autism, active since 2019, that advocates for public policy, runs family support and training, and organizes the annual 'Paraguay Runs for Autism' event.
initiatives.notes: Parent/guardian-led, not self-advocate-led. Affiliated with the Autism Latin America Federation (ALaFe). President as of 2024-2026: Diana Villalba.

initiatives.name: Peruvian Autistic People's Association (APEAU)
initiatives.summary: A Lima-based nonprofit founded in 2023 and composed exclusively of autistic members, advocating for autistic people's rights under the motto 'nada sobre nosotros sin nosotros' and organizing community events in Peru.
initiatives.notes: The domain asociacionperuanadeautistas.com surfaced in search results but did not resolve on repeated checks; using their active Instagram (posts through late 2025, includes Hispanoamerican Autism Congress participation) as url/source_url instead. Also active on Facebook.

initiatives.name: Teatro La Plaza
initiatives.summary: Theatre in Lima, Peru, founded in 2003 by a group of artists including director Chela De Ferrari (non-disabled); internationally known for productions 'Hamlet' (2021) and 'Ricardo III' (2023), which cast actors with Down syndrome.
initiatives.notes: General theatre venue directed by non-disabled founder; Down-syndrome casting applies to specific acclaimed productions, not a standing disabled ensemble. Site blocks some browser user-agents (403 on one UA, 200 on another) — confirmed live either way.

initiatives.name: Autism Society Philippines (ASP)
initiatives.summary: National nonprofit founded in 1989 with about 16,000 members across 106 local chapters, working toward social acceptance and self-reliance for autistic Filipinos.

initiatives.name: Autism-Poland Coalition
initiatives.summary: A Warsaw-based coalition of Polish autism organisations doing national advocacy, running an information centre and legal support, and promoting supported-housing 'Home Communities' for autistic adults.
initiatives.notes: Listed as 'Autism Poland Association' in Autism-Europe's August 2026 member directory; office shares an address with the Synapsis Foundation in Warsaw. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

initiatives.name: Fundacja ADHD
initiatives.summary: Polish foundation providing psychological consultations, ADHD and autism diagnostic assessments, crisis support and public education for neurodivergent people nationwide.
initiatives.notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations. No single headquarters city stated.

initiatives.name: Fundacja Autism Team
initiatives.summary: Łódź-based Polish foundation, founded 2016, combining autistic people, families, experts and therapists to run youth and parent support clubs, crisis intervention, school inclusion programmes and creative 'Artegracja' projects.
initiatives.notes: Site describes staff as 'osoby w spektrum autyzmu, ich rodziny, eksperci i terapeuci' (autistic people, their families, experts and therapists), hence marked mixed rather than nd-led.

initiatives.name: Jasna Strona Spektrum
initiatives.summary: Polish autism information and support website for diagnosed and undiagnosed autistic children and adults, publishing articles on daily life, self-advocacy and diagnosis and running parent workshops.
initiatives.notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Leadership not stated on the site; no fixed city given.

initiatives.name: JiM Foundation
initiatives.summary: A Łódź-based Polish foundation running diagnostic and therapy clinics and schools for autistic and ADHD children, offering free screening, legal aid, and public campaigns such as 'Quiet Hours'.
initiatives.notes: Registered in Poland's National Court Register (KRS 0000127075). Listed as an Autism-Europe affiliated member. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

initiatives.name: Polish Dyslexia Society (PTD)
initiatives.summary: Polish learned society on dyslexia running regional branches, an advisory clinic, and courses and training on specific learning difficulties, with an active branch in Gdańsk.
initiatives.notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Site is mostly navigation/image-based; national headquarters not clearly stated, so located at its documented Gdańsk branch.

initiatives.name: Synapsis Foundation
initiatives.summary: A Warsaw foundation running diagnostic and therapy centres for autistic children and adults, plus Poland's first social enterprise and training home for autistic adults, and training for specialists and parents.
initiatives.notes: The domain listed for Synapsis in Autism-Europe's official directory (synapsis.waw.pl) is now a dead placeholder page; synapsis.org.pl is the current live site. Site references a 20th-anniversary milestone in 2026 for one of its centres, but the foundation's own founding year is not directly confirmed.

initiatives.name: Brainstorm
initiatives.summary: A Portuguese self-advocacy association founded by and for people with ADHD (PHDA) that runs peer WhatsApp communities and campaigns for a more informed, neuro-inclusive society.
initiatives.notes: Founded 2024, publicly launched 2025. No confirmed physical headquarters was found; it operates nationally online, so Lisbon is used only as an approximate anchor point.

initiatives.name: Dislex
initiatives.summary: A Portuguese association founded by academics and clinicians that researches dyslexia, provides adult self-assessment tools and resources for families, and campaigns for teacher training on dyslexia.
initiatives.notes: Founded by researchers and clinicians including Vítor da Fonseca; run by a professional board rather than by dyslexic people themselves. Has publicly criticised lack of teacher training for dyslexia support.

initiatives.name: Mad in Portugal
initiatives.summary: Portuguese affiliate of the Mad in the World network, publishing critical-psychiatry journalism and lived-experience writing in Portuguese.
initiatives.region: Lisbon (national scope; editorial base not stated)
initiatives.notes: Part of the Mad in the World network.

initiatives.name: Ouvir Vozes Movement Portugal
initiatives.summary: Portugal's national hearing-voices movement, publishing peer information and coping strategies via a WordPress blog, listed as Portugal's Intervoice contact.
initiatives.notes: Distinct from the editorial site Mad in Portugal, also in this file.

initiatives.name: Voz do Autista (APVA)
initiatives.summary: Aveiro-based self-advocacy association of autistic adults, parents and autistic health/education professionals, running an online rights-guidance service, employment support projects and free resources for autistic people.
initiatives.notes: Full member of EUCAP. Describes itself as 'an association of autists, for autists.'

initiatives.name: Mad in Puerto Rico
initiatives.summary: Puerto Rican affiliate of the Mad in the World network, publishing critical-psychiatry journalism and lived-experience writing in Spanish for a Puerto Rican audience.
initiatives.region: San Juan (national scope; editorial base not stated)
initiatives.notes: Part of the Mad in the World network; distinct from the older Mad in America Hispanohablante / Mad in (S)pain lineage.

initiatives.name: Help Autism
initiatives.summary: Romania's largest autism organisation, founded around 2010 and based in Bucharest, running eight therapy centres nationwide, a digital platform for specialists and families, and inclusive camps and sports programmes.
initiatives.notes: Founded and led by Daniela Bololoi; run by professionals and specialists rather than a self-advocacy model. Listed as an Autism-Europe affiliated member. Founding year inferred from a '16 years' reference on the site as of February 2026.

initiatives.name: suntAutist
initiatives.summary: Romanian association publishing 'autism explained by autistics' articles by autistic contributors, opposing ABA and conversion-style therapies and offering resources for autistic children, women and men.
initiatives.notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Tagline 'Autismul explicat de autiști' (autism explained by autistics); named autistic contributors write the site's articles. No fixed city stated.

initiatives.name: Prostor
initiatives.summary: A Serbian mental-health NGO running peer creative workshops, mental-health campaigns and volunteering programmes with people who use psychiatric services; Serbia's node of the Balkan Voices hearing-voices network.
initiatives.region: Novi Sad (approximate; exact city not stated on site)
initiatives.notes: City is an approximation from general knowledge of the organisation, not confirmed on its own about page; a moderator should verify.

initiatives.name: Union of Serbian Autism Associations
initiatives.name_local: Savez udruženja Srbije za pomoć osobama sa autizmom
initiatives.summary: A Belgrade-based union of member associations from across Serbia that raises public awareness of autism and seeks systemic legal and policy solutions for autistic people's rights.
