initiatives.notes: Listed as 'Serbian Society for Autism' in Autism-Europe's August 2026 member directory. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

initiatives.name: Autism Resource Centre (Singapore)
initiatives.summary: Singapore charity registered in 2000 providing lifelong services for autistic people, including Pathlight School, early intervention, employment support, and caregiver training.
initiatives.notes: Runs Pathlight School, Singapore's first autism-focused school.

initiatives.name: A Centrum
initiatives.summary: Slovak organisation running education, conferences and a self-advocacy programme ('Kľúče k sebaobhajobe') on autism, Asperger syndrome and neurodiversity, involving neurodivergent young people as volunteers and advocates.
initiatives.notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Leads courses/podcasts through Viera Hincová; not explicitly stated whether the organisation itself is autistic-led.

initiatives.name: S.P.O.S.A. (Slovak Autism Society)
initiatives.name_local: Spoločnosť na pomoc osobám s autizmom
initiatives.summary: A Bratislava-based Slovak national association offering autism education, counselling, a virtual-reality autism simulator, and the 'Autists at Work' employment training programme.
initiatives.notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Site footer shows a 2016 copyright year, which may not reflect the organisation's actual founding date; leadership composition not stated.

initiatives.name: Association of NGOs for Autism Slovenia
initiatives.summary: A Slovenian national association bringing together NGOs working on autism, listed as an Autism-Europe affiliated member representing the country's autism community.
initiatives.notes: The site returns an automated bot-verification page to scripted requests, so it could not be read directly; its existence and role are confirmed via Autism-Europe's official August 2026 member directory. Founding year and leadership composition unconfirmed.

initiatives.name: Mad in Slovenia
initiatives.summary: Slovenian affiliate of the Mad in the World network, launched in spring 2025, publishing critical-psychiatry articles, professional contributions and a resource page for relatives; grew to over 70 members by December 2025.
initiatives.region: Ljubljana (national scope; editorial base not stated)
initiatives.notes: One of the newest Mad in the World affiliates as of this writing.

initiatives.name: Autism South Africa
initiatives.summary: National non-profit providing information, guidance, training, and advocacy for autistic people and their families across South Africa's nine provinces.
initiatives.notes: Registered Public Benefit Organisation; leadership structure not stated on site.

initiatives.name: AMATDAH
initiatives.name_local: Asociación Madrileña de Adultos con TDAH
initiatives.summary: A Madrid association run by and for adults diagnosed with ADHD, which grew out of patient meetings at a specialty clinic, offering peer support and pressing institutions on adult ADHD rights.
initiatives.notes: Grew out of peer meetings among patients at Madrid's Centro de Especialidades Argüelles from 2012. amatdah.org returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited) on repeated automated checks in this session; existence and current activity were confirmed via the SID-INICO and SOM360 directories instead.

initiatives.name: CEPAMA (Committee for the Promotion and Support of Autistic Girls and Women)
initiatives.name_local: Comité para la Promoción y Apoyo de las Niñas y Mujeres Autistas
initiatives.summary: Spanish association of autistic women working on the rights, visibility and research access of autistic girls and women, including a participatory research project with the University of Lisbon on employment, education and healthcare.
initiatives.notes: Full member of EUCAP. Site states 'somos mujeres autistas' (we are autistic women) and describes governance by autistic women.

initiatives.name: Debajo del Sombrero
initiatives.summary: Debajo del Sombrero is a Madrid nonprofit platform, active since 2007, running an assisted art studio and gallery where professional staff accompany artists with intellectual disabilities in creating, exhibiting, and selling contemporary art.
initiatives.notes: debajodelsombrero.org (alternate domain) timed out on curl (20s connection timeout) and was not used; debajodelsombrero.es returned 200 OK. 2007 founding date is from third-party arts-press coverage (masdearte.com, mediacionartistica.org) found before search quota ran out, not an explicit dated claim on the official site itself.

initiatives.name: Mad Pride Madrid (Orgullo Loco)
initiatives.summary: A Madrid psychiatric-survivor collective organising around Mad Pride, publishing a blog on mental-health activism, deinstitutionalization and reclaiming madness as identity rather than illness.
initiatives.notes: Part of the same Latin/Iberian Orgullo Loco movement as the Buenos Aires and Chile entries already in the atlas.

initiatives.name: Autism Sverige
initiatives.summary: Sweden's national autism federation, based in Stockholm and organised into district associations, providing information, an ombudsman service, policy advocacy, and a training centre for professionals and families.
initiatives.notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

initiatives.name: Dyslexiförbundet
initiatives.summary: Swedish national federation for people with dyslexia and dyscalculia, based in Stockholm, offering educational and workplace guidance, a writing-support helpline, assistive-technology information and a member magazine.
initiatives.notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Patron is Prince Carl Philip of Sweden.

initiatives.name: Mad in Sweden
initiatives.summary: Swedish affiliate of the Mad in the World network, publishing critical-psychiatry journalism, research summaries and therapy-policy commentary in Swedish.
initiatives.region: Stockholm (national scope; editorial base not stated)
initiatives.notes: Part of the Mad in the World network.

initiatives.name: Organiserade Autister
initiatives.summary: Swedish interest association of and for autistic people (formerly known as Organiserade Aspergare), running discussion groups and community activities and promoting neurodiversity and self-determination.
initiatives.notes: Full member of EUCAP. Site describes itself as 'an interest association of and for autists.' Likely the current name of the organisation previously known as Organiserade Aspergare; no fixed city stated.

initiatives.name: Autism Switzerland
initiatives.summary: A Zurich-based Swiss network organisation providing an autism information platform, a nationwide directory of specialised services by canton, therapeutic training, and public-awareness campaigns.
initiatives.notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Operates alongside partner organisations for French- and Italian-speaking Switzerland (including Autisme Suisse Romande). Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

initiatives.name: Collection de l'Art Brut
initiatives.summary: The founding art brut museum, opened 1976 in Château de Beaulieu, Lausanne, from Jean Dubuffet's 1971 donation of ~5,000 works to the city; now holds over 60,000 pieces.
initiatives.notes: Curatorial institution run by the City of Lausanne, not artist-led. Many original works came from psychiatric patients, but the collection deliberately spans self-taught/marginal creators beyond that population.

initiatives.name: Netzwerk Stimmenhören Schweiz (Swiss Hearing Voices Network)
initiatives.summary: Switzerland's national Hearing Voices Network, coordinating peer groups and information for voice-hearers and listed as Switzerland's Intervoice contact.

initiatives.name: Theater HORA
initiatives.summary: Zurich ensemble theatre founded in 1993 by Michael Elber, part of Stiftung Züriwerk since 2002; all ensemble actors have a certified cognitive/learning disability, while artistic and overall direction is held by non-disabled staff.
initiatives.notes: 18 full-time ensemble actors are IV-certified with cognitive disability; overall/artistic direction is non-disabled. 'Freie Republik HORA' lab (since 2013) lets ensemble members direct/choreograph their own work.

initiatives.name: Autism Society of Taiwan
initiatives.summary: National civic association based in Taipei serving autistic people and families, running vocational and social training as well as diagnostic and employment support.
initiatives.notes: Runs the 'Star Kids Workshop' vocational and social training programme.

initiatives.name: The Association of Parent for Thai Persons with Autism
initiatives.name_local: สมาคมผู้ปกครองบุคคลออทิซึม (ไทย)
initiatives.summary: Bangkok-based nonprofit working alongside the Autistic Thai Foundation on quality-of-life programmes for autistic people, including sports, digital learning, and IT skills training.
initiatives.notes: Parent association; partners with the government-accredited Autistic Thai Foundation.

initiatives.name: Denizli Autism Association (DOD)
initiatives.summary: A rights-based Turkish civil-society organisation in Denizli, founded around 2016, publishing reports on discrimination against autistic people, offering family counselling, and sitting on the Turkish Autism Council.
initiatives.notes: Autism-Europe affiliated member; its General Secretary sits on the Autism-Europe Board of Directors. A regional rather than national body, distinct from the Turkish national anchor organisation Tohum Otizm already in this dataset. Founding year inferred from a '10th anniversary' reference in recent site news.

initiatives.name: Tohum Otizm Vakfı (Tohum Autism Foundation)
initiatives.summary: Istanbul-based public-benefit foundation focused on early diagnosis and special education for autistic children, and on national autism screening and awareness campaigns.

initiatives.name: Autism Awareness Uganda
initiatives.summary: Kampala-based community organisation of parents, professionals, and volunteers running caregiver training, awareness campaigns, and referral support for autistic people.

initiatives.name: Child With Future
initiatives.summary: A Kyiv-based Ukrainian foundation, active since around 2011, running a developmental kindergarten and international autism conferences, and representing Ukraine on Autism-Europe's board since 2012.
initiatives.notes: Autism-Europe affiliated member. Founding year inferred from a '15 years' reference on the site; leadership composition not stated.

initiatives.name: Dubai Autism Center
initiatives.summary: UAE nonprofit established by government decree providing assessment, intervention, rehabilitation, and community-awareness programs for autistic children.

initiatives.name: ARGH Scotland
initiatives.summary: Scottish charitable incorporated organisation based in the Highlands whose committee and full voting members are all autistic, doing collective advocacy, lobbying and campaigning on autism services across Scotland.
initiatives.notes: Full member of EUCAP. The listed EUCAP URL (arghscotland.co.uk) now redirects permanently to arghscotland.org, used here. Partners with the Scottish Government on autism strategy.

initiatives.name: Autistic Mutual Aid Society Edinburgh (AMASE)
initiatives.summary: Edinburgh-based Autistic People's Organisation whose full members are all autistic, running peer support, an online 'My Autism Story' event series, Autistic Pride and Weird Pride Day gatherings, and policy statements.
initiatives.notes: Full member of EUCAP. Site states 'all full members are autistic.' Most events run online.

initiatives.name: Autistic UK
initiatives.summary: A community interest company run by autistic adults across Wales, England and Scotland that campaigns on policy, publishes position statements, and builds peer networks for autistic people.
initiatives.notes: Operated as an unincorporated voluntary organisation from 2009, then incorporated as a CIC in 2019 (registered office Caernarfon, Wales, per Companies House).

initiatives.name: Autscape
initiatives.summary: An annual multi-day conference run by and for autistic people, with workshops, social time and sensory-considered spaces, organised by a UK registered charity.
initiatives.notes: Registered UK charity since 2011; most organisers are autistic. Venue varies by year, recently High Leigh in Hoddesdon; some years run as an online-only edition.

initiatives.name: Bethlem Museum of the Mind
initiatives.summary: Museum of mental health history and patient art on the grounds of Bethlem Royal Hospital (Beckenham), opened in its current Art Deco building in March 2015 as the public face of the Bethlem Art and History Collections Trust (est. 1970).
initiatives.notes: Run by the hospital-linked charitable trust; archive/collection roots go back to 1970. Distinct from the separate Bethlem Gallery, which is more directly artist-facing.

initiatives.name: Blue Apple Theatre
initiatives.summary: Winchester, UK theatre company founded in 2005 by Jane Jessop, producing theatre, dance, singing and film with performers who have learning disabilities; operates as a working name of the Minstead Trust charity.
initiatives.notes: Founded by Jane Jessop (non-disabled), mother of company member Tommy Jessop, who has Down syndrome; site separates 'Performers' from 'Staff/Facilitators/Trustees'.

initiatives.name: British Dyslexia Association (BDA)
initiatives.summary: English registered charity providing dyslexia and dyscalculia assessments, teacher training and accreditation, a helpline, and a Dyslexia Friendly Quality Mark for schools and workplaces.
initiatives.notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Registered charity 289243.

initiatives.name: DaDaFest
initiatives.summary: Biennial disability and Deaf arts festival in Liverpool produced by DaDa, a self-described disability-controlled/disability-led arts organisation with roots to 1984; the festival launched in 2001.
initiatives.notes: Parent org DaDa traces roots to 1984 (as Arts Integrated Merseyside/North West Disability Arts Forum); DaDaFest festival itself began 2001.

initiatives.name: Flow Observatorium
initiatives.summary: An equality and diversity charity and creative hub for neurodivergent artists in Portsmouth, running free co-creation sessions and training arts organisations to be neurodivergent-enabling.
initiatives.notes: Founded with Arts Council England funding, led by neurodivergent artist Jon Adams with Donna Bish. Runs 'KoCreate' sessions with Portsmouth Autism Community Forum. Site is hosted on Wix and may change address.

initiatives.name: Hearing Voices Network (England)
initiatives.summary: A small national charity, run mostly by volunteers, that supports and connects local peer-support groups across England for people who hear voices, see visions or have other unusual perceptions.
initiatives.notes: Does not run local groups directly, only supports and networks them; work is carried out mostly by volunteers including trustees. Exact founding year not confirmed on-site.

initiatives.name: Heart n Soul
initiatives.summary: South East London arts organisation making music and performance work, originating from 1984 creative sessions in Lewisham and formally founded 1987; explicitly led by people with and without learning disabilities and autistic people.
initiatives.notes: Founding date varies across sources (1984 workshops, 1986 performance company, 1987 per Shape Arts timeline); leadership language ('led by people with and without learning disabilities and autistic people') is the org's own self-description.

initiatives.name: Hijinx Theatre
initiatives.summary: Cardiff-based inclusive theatre company founded in 1981 by Gaynor Lougher and Richard Berry; centers learning disabled and/or autistic artists as its core ensemble, currently under co-CEOs Ben Pettitt-Wade and Eloise Tong.
initiatives.notes: Founders and current leadership are not disclosed as disabled; org's own language centers learning disabled/autistic artists as creative contributors without stating they hold governance roles.

initiatives.name: Mad in the UK
initiatives.summary: British affiliate of the Mad in the World network, publishing critical-psychiatry journalism, blogs and 'around the web' roundups since 2018, distinct from the earlier-founded Mad in Ireland.
initiatives.region: London, England (national scope; editorial base not stated)
initiatives.notes: About page returned 403 to automated requests; founding confirmed instead via the site's own 2018 welcome post.

initiatives.name: Mind the Gap
initiatives.summary: Bradford-based learning disability and autism performance and live-arts company founded in 1988 by Tim Wheeler and Susan Brown; learning disabled and autistic artists co-create productions and help steer the company's creative work.
initiatives.notes: Site states artists 'directly influence and steer' the work and its vision is a world where 'learning disabled and autistic voices lead the way' — aspirational/future-tense, not a present-tense 'led by' claim. Current joint CEOs show no disability disclosure.

initiatives.name: National Autistic Taskforce (NAT)
initiatives.summary: British autistic-run body, founded 2018, that campaigns for better services for autistic people with high support needs, publishing independent care-quality guides and running the EQUALS Project on decision-making support.
initiatives.notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Describes itself as 'an innovative autistic-run body' focused on autistic people less able to self-advocate. No single headquarters city stated; placed at London as a national placeholder.

initiatives.name: National Survivor User Network (NSUN)
initiatives.summary: England's national lived-experience-led mental health charity, connecting and amplifying people with lived experience of mental distress and user-led grassroots groups, based in London.
initiatives.notes: Self-describes as 'England's only lived experience-led national mental health charity'. Registered address: 483 Green Lanes, London N13 4BS.

initiatives.name: Neuk Collective
initiatives.summary: Scotland-wide community and advocacy network for neurodivergent artists, run under Door in the Wall Arts Access CIC (a disabled-led organisation) and founded by neurodivergent textile artist Tzipporah Johnston.
initiatives.notes: Exact founding year not stated on the site (its own 'Our story'/'history' subpages 404'd during verification); currently active with a directory, membership, and a 2026 Glasgow exhibition.

initiatives.name: Oska Bright Film Festival
initiatives.summary: Biennial film festival in Brighton founded in 2004 by learning-disabled filmmakers, screening only films made by or featuring learning-disabled and/or autistic people, run today by a learning-disabled programming team under Carousel.

initiatives.name: Participatory Autism Research Collective (PARC)
initiatives.summary: A voluntary UK network, started at London South Bank University, that brings autistic scholars and activists together with early-career researchers to promote autistic involvement in autism research.
initiatives.notes: Co-founded by Damian Milton and Nicola Martin; first meeting April 2015. Now spans several UK institutions including Birmingham, Sheffield Hallam and Nottingham. Active in 2026 per site events listing.

initiatives.name: Raw Vision
initiatives.summary: Quarterly print and online magazine devoted to outsider art and art brut, founded by John Maizels in London in 1989 and now headquartered in Radlett, Hertfordshire.
initiatives.notes: Edited/founded by art historian John Maizels, not by neurodivergent or disabled staff explicitly.

initiatives.name: Recovery in the Bin (RITB)
initiatives.summary: A UK critical-theorist and activist collective that critiques mainstream 'recovery' models in mental health, publishing survivor-led frameworks like the '#Neorecovery' critique and the Unrecovery Star.
initiatives.region: United Kingdom (online collective; no fixed city stated)
initiatives.notes: Site explicitly publishes a piece titled '#Neorecovery: A Survivor Led Conceptualisation and Critique', supporting the nd-led designation.

initiatives.name: Scottish ADHD Coalition
initiatives.summary: Scottish charity, founded 2017 out of a 2016 Dundee meeting of local groups, coordinating voluntary organisations across Scotland that support adults and children with ADHD, including youth groups, parent training and referral information.
initiatives.notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations, though the coalition itself dates to 2017. Registered Scottish charity SC047320.

initiatives.name: Scottish Autism
initiatives.summary: Scotland's largest autism-specific service provider, founded in 1968 by a group of parents, running residential and day support, an advice line, family support and participatory research through its Centre for Practice, Policy and Research.
initiatives.notes: Included as a large, well-known ally-led anchor organisation for Scotland, in contrast to the autistic-led ARGH Scotland and AMASE entries in this batch.

initiatives.name: Soteria Network UK
initiatives.summary: A UK network of service users, survivors, carers, activists and professionals promoting the drug-free or minimum-medication Soteria House model for people experiencing psychosis.
initiatives.region: United Kingdom (online network; no fixed city stated)
initiatives.notes: Self-describes as part of 'an international movement of service users, survivors, activists, carers, academics and professionals'.

initiatives.name: Survivor Researcher Network
initiatives.summary: A UK network for and by psychiatric-survivor and service-user researchers, hosted by the National Survivor User Network (NSUN), supporting peer-led mental-health research and skill-sharing.
initiatives.notes: Operates as a programme of NSUN, also in this file, rather than as a separately incorporated organisation.

initiatives.name: The Museum of Everything
initiatives.summary: UK registered charity and travelling museum for self-taught, art brut and outsider art, founded by James Brett in London in 2009; operates the Gallery of Everything, its commercial space on Chiltern Street.
initiatives.notes: Site 301-redirects to musevery.com (HTTP 200). Curated by founder James Brett, not by ND/disabled people themselves. Touring model plus fixed Gallery of Everything retail space; recent (2025/26) exhibition dates not independently confirmed.

initiatives.name: Unlimited
initiatives.summary: UK commissioning body backing new work by disabled artists since 2012, delivered in partnership by disability-led charity Shape Arts and producer Artsadmin, staging periodic festivals in London.
initiatives.notes: Originally conceived by Arts Council England for the 2012 Cultural Olympiad; delivery partnership pairs disability-led Shape Arts with Artsadmin, which is not disability-led per available sources — hence 'mixed' rather than 'nd-led'.

initiatives.name: Academic Autism Spectrum Partnership in Research and Education
initiatives.summary: Community-based participatory research partnership, based at Portland State University, in which autistic adults are equal partners with academics. Known for work on healthcare access and other autistic-adult priorities.
initiatives.notes: Long-standing partner of the Autistic Self Advocacy Network and Autism Society of Oregon; the /about-us/ page returned a 404 during this check, verified instead via the homepage and third-party coverage.

initiatives.name: Arts of Life
initiatives.summary: Chicago nonprofit founded in 2000 providing studio space, art supplies, and exhibition and sales support to artists with intellectual and developmental disabilities, with additional studios on Chicago's North Shore.

initiatives.name: Autistic Self Advocacy Network
initiatives.summary: National advocacy organization run by and for autistic people, founded in 2006. Works on disability policy, public education, and community organizing around autism rights in the United States.

initiatives.name: Autistic Women & Nonbinary Network
initiatives.summary: Peer network and resource hub for autistic women, transgender, and nonbinary people, run by and for autistic people. Provides community support, publications, and advocacy from its base in Lincoln, Nebraska.

initiatives.name: CHADD (Children and Adults with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder)
initiatives.summary: National nonprofit headquartered in Lanham, Maryland, that runs a federally funded National Resource Center on ADHD, publishes Attention magazine, and coordinates local support chapters for people with ADHD and their families.
initiatives.notes: Commonly reported elsewhere as founded in 1987 by parents of children with ADHD; not independently confirmed on the current site during this pass, so left null.

initiatives.name: Creative Growth Art Center
initiatives.summary: Studio and gallery in Oakland founded in 1973 where adult artists with developmental, intellectual, and physical disabilities make and sell visual art. One of the earliest organizations of its kind in the United States.
initiatives.notes: Founding date is given as 1973 or 1974 in different sources; founded by educator Florence Ludins-Katz and psychologist Elias Katz.

initiatives.name: Creativity Explored
initiatives.summary: Creativity Explored is a San Francisco studio founded in 1983 by Florence Ludins-Katz and Elias Katz that gives adults with developmental disabilities studio access, materials, and professional support to create and sell art.
initiatives.notes: Curl 200 OK. Site language is 'partners with artists with developmental disabilities'; run by professional staff, not artist-governed.

initiatives.name: Fireweed Collective
initiatives.summary: Peer-led network for people who identify as mad, crazy, or mentally ill, founded in 2002 as the Icarus Project and renamed in 2020. Runs peer support groups, workshops, and trainings centering disabled, Black, and queer communities.
initiatives.notes: Formerly the Icarus Project; restructured and renamed in 2020 to foreground Black, disabled, immigrant, and queer/trans leadership.

initiatives.name: Foundations for Divergent Minds
initiatives.summary: Texas-based nonprofit founded and led by multiply neurodivergent autistic people, providing online neurodiversity education, healthcare-access programming, and violence-prevention work for autistic communities.

initiatives.name: Hearing Voices Network USA
initiatives.summary: The USA's national Hearing Voices Network, coordinating peer support groups, training and a resource directory for voice-hearers across the country.
initiatives.region: Northampton, MA (approximate; site did not state a fixed HQ)
initiatives.notes: Site blocked most automated requests with HTTP 429/403; a plain GET without www eventually returned HTTP 202. Region is an approximate placeholder in western Massachusetts, historically a hub of US peer/HV organising; a moderator should confirm the network's actual current base.

initiatives.name: LAND Gallery
initiatives.summary: LAND Studio & Gallery is a nonprofit day-habilitation program in Brooklyn, NY, founded in 2005 by the League Education and Treatment Center, teaching life skills through art alongside professional artists.

initiatives.name: MindFreedom International
initiatives.summary: Coalition of grassroots groups founded in 1990 by psychiatric survivors, based in Eugene, Oregon. Advocates against forced psychiatric treatment and for human rights and alternatives in mental health care.
initiatives.notes: Membership is majority psychiatric survivors; site states MFI "was started by psychiatric survivors."

initiatives.name: NIAD Art Center
initiatives.summary: NIAD Art Center is a nonprofit studio in Richmond, California for adult artists with developmental and physical disabilities, founded in 1982, where staff support artists in creating and selling work.
initiatives.notes: www.niadart.org 301-redirects to niadart.org (final 200 OK, curl-verified). Site does not state a leadership model explicitly.

initiatives.name: Passion Works Studio
initiatives.summary: Passion Works Studio is a nonprofit collaborative art studio in Athens, Ohio, creating paid creative work for artists with and without developmental disabilities, best known for its handmade Passion Flowers.
initiatives.notes: Founding year not stated on official pages checked (site references '20 years' of undated copy and Patty Mitchell working there 'since 1994'); could not independently verify this session. 'mixed' leadership reflects the site's own framing as 'creative people with and without developmental differences' working collaboratively, plus 'we wanted to create an organization that follows the lead, talent and interests of our artists.'

initiatives.name: Project Onward
initiatives.summary: Project Onward is a nonprofit studio and gallery in Chicago, founded in 2004 out of the city's Gallery 37 youth program, providing studio space, materials, and career support to more than 60 adult artists with disabilities and mental illness.

initiatives.name: Pure Vision Arts
initiatives.summary: Pure Vision Arts is a studio and exhibition space in New York City, founded in 2002 as a program of The Shield Institute, staffed by art-education and art-therapy professionals who support artists with autism and other developmental disabilities.
initiatives.notes: purevisionarts.org 301-redirects to www.purevisionarts.org (final 200 OK, curl-verified).

initiatives.name: ReelAbilities Film Festival: New York
initiatives.summary: Film festival dedicated to disability representation on and off screen, founded in 2007 at the Marlene Meyerson JCC Manhattan and now the flagship of a touring ReelAbilities network across the US.
initiatives.notes: Leadership marked unknown: available sources name JCC Manhattan and co-directors but do not state whether disabled people hold leadership/staff roles.

initiatives.name: Stanford Neurodiversity Project
initiatives.summary: Program at Stanford Medicine, recently renamed the Stanford Center for Neurodiversity and Human Potential, running education, employment, and research initiatives for autistic and other neurodivergent people.
initiatives.notes: Name is in transition from "Stanford Neurodiversity Project" to "Stanford Center for Neurodiversity and Human Potential"; both names appear on Stanford's own pages.

initiatives.name: Superfest International Disability Film Festival
initiatives.summary: Longest-running disability film festival in the world, founded in 1970, now produced by the Paul K. Longmore Institute on Disability and the San Francisco Disability Cultural Center in the Bay Area.
initiatives.notes: Leadership marked unknown: sources confirm disabled people serve as judges but do not explicitly state staff/leadership disability status.

initiatives.name: The Art of Autism
initiatives.summary: San Diego-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit, founded 2005, that promotes autistic artists via an online gallery, exhibits and film festivals; states its board is approximately 50% autistic.
initiatives.notes: Explicitly self-reports ~50% autistic board composition on its own fact sheet; active with content through August 2026.

initiatives.name: The Color of Autism Foundation
initiatives.summary: Detroit-area nonprofit founded in 2009 by a parent of an autistic child, providing culturally specific autism support, training, and a support group for Black fathers and co-parents of autistic children.
initiatives.notes: Registered address is in Beverly Hills, MI (metro Detroit); the organization describes its direct-service base as Detroit families.

initiatives.name: The Neurodiversity Alliance (Eye to Eye)
initiatives.summary: New York-based nonprofit, formerly known as Eye to Eye, founded by and for people with learning disabilities and ADHD, that runs a national school-based mentoring program pairing older and younger students who learn differently.
initiatives.notes: Formerly Eye to Eye; eyetoeyenational.org now redirects to thendalliance.org. Sources vary between ~20 and ~25 years since founding, so an exact year is left null.

initiatives.name: Visionaries + Voices
initiatives.summary: Nonprofit studio in Cincinnati, founded in 2003, offering visual art space, materials, and exhibition opportunities to more than 125 artists with disabilities.

initiatives.name: Aletea
initiatives.name_local: Aletea - Asociación civil uruguaya para el colectivo autista
initiatives.summary: A Montevideo civil association of families and professionals working for the social inclusion of autistic people in Uruguay from a neurodiversity and social-model-of-disability framework, offering training, multidisciplinary support and advocacy.
initiatives.notes: Family- and professional-run rather than self-advocacy-led, but explicitly adopts the neurodiversity paradigm.

initiatives.name: Radio Vilardevoz / Mad Pride Uruguay
initiatives.summary: A psychiatric-survivor-led community radio and cultural project born in 1997 at the Vilardebó psychiatric hospital in Montevideo, now running a cultural space and organizing Uruguay's Mad Pride marches against institutionalization and electroshock.
initiatives.notes: Ran Uruguay's first Mad Pride march in Plaza Independencia, September 21, 2023; site active with posts through September 2026.

initiatives.name: RUATDAH (Uruguayan ADHD Support Network)
initiatives.name_local: Red Uruguaya de Apoyo al TDAH
initiatives.summary: A family-led Uruguayan network created because no organization previously existed to support people with ADHD, providing information, guidance and community for families and advocating for better public policy on diagnosis and treatment.
initiatives.notes: Explicitly family-run rather than adult-ADHD self-advocacy; site actively maintained with recent articles and event promotion.

initiatives.name: Vietnam Autism Network (VAN)
initiatives.name_local: Mạng lưới Tự kỷ Việt Nam
initiatives.summary: Voluntary nonprofit network of parents, autism specialists, and autistic individuals recognised by Vietnam's Ministry of Labour, running national autism awareness activities.
initiatives.notes: Governing board is elected from parent-group representatives across six provinces/cities; member of the ASEAN Autism Network.
